desk.headline: Revenue $3.0m and adjusted loss of $0.44 a share, both below estimates; Serra Verde shipments start, Q4 volume target of 325+ tonnes

other.label: Net income (GAAP)
other.change: lifted by a $136.6m fair-value gain; diluted EPS -$0.02

results: Revenue was only $3.0m, with cost of revenue of $22.9m leaving a gross loss of about $20m.
Operating loss widened to $141m as SG&A jumped to $104m after the Serra Verde deal closed in September.
A $137m gain on warrant and earnout liabilities turned the GAAP result into an $11.7m profit; the adjusted loss was $126m, or $0.44 a share.
Serra Verde in Brazil finished Stage 1 on time and on budget; Stillwater made its first commercial magnet sales.
Cash stood at $1.16bn; the balance sheet now carries about $306m of notes and $362m of royalty obligations from Serra Verde.

guidance.summary: No revenue or profit guidance. For Q4 the company expects Serra Verde to sell at least 325 tonnes of rare earth oxides and set project milestones through end-2027, including a 6,400 tpa run rate at Serra Verde.

points: Management blamed the drop in sales from about $6m a quarter on shortages of dysprosium oxide and samarium metal.
Several timelines slipped, including the Round Top technical report (now Q3 2027) and Stillwater Line 1b (now Q2 2027).
The finance chief did not reaffirm the earlier $550-650m exit-2027 EBITDA run-rate target.
Serra Verde Stage 2 is about 40% built, and magnet letters of intent total about 2,500 tonnes.
New CEO Thras Moraitis split the group into upstream, midstream and downstream units and linked expansion pace to feedstock and demand.
call.source: Call coverage: USA Rare Earth misses badly as the Serra Verde production pivot arrives — Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 9 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Serra Verde delivers at least 325 tonnes in Q4 and ramps toward 4,000 tpa.
Cash burn against the $1.16bn balance as start-up costs flow through.
